problem_framing.title: Framing guidance
problem_framing.body: Write the problem without naming a model. AI suitability and EU tier are outputs of this phase, not assumptions.
tips: Prefer placeholder names for clients and systems
Capture who decides go or no-go

data_discovery.title: Data discovery guidance
data_discovery.body: Data state is the strongest timeline driver. Inventory before architecture.
tips: Estimate labelling as its own workstream

solution_architecture.title: Architecture guidance
solution_architecture.body: Compare options against data reality. Include monitoring and human oversight in the design, not as a postscript.

data_engineering.title: Data engineering guidance
data_engineering.body: Feature definitions often change after the first model cycles. Plan for partial re-runs.

model_development.title: Model development guidance
model_development.body: Expect 5 to 20 training cycles. Done means the model beats an agreed baseline on held-out data, not that one experiment finished.
tips: Freeze the evaluation protocol before comparing models
Iterative nature is normal — schedule capacity for rework

validation_testing.title: Validation guidance
validation_testing.body: AI testing includes bias, edge cases, and silent failure modes that unit tests never catch.
tips: Include regulatory evidence in the pack

deployment.title: Deployment guidance
deployment.body: Prefer shadow and canary before full traffic. Monitoring activation is part of go-live, not a follow-up ticket.

hypercare.title: Hypercare guidance
hypercare.body: Hypercare is ongoing. Models drift. Plan retraining budget and ownership before go-live.
tips: Define drift alerts and retrain triggers in writing

t_baseline.body: A weak baseline still counts. Random, majority class, or simple rules show whether ML is earning its keep.

t_training_cycles.body: Treat each cycle as a hypothesis test. Stop when budget or diminishing returns say so.

t_drift_monitor.body: Monitor both input distributions and outcome quality. One without the other is a blind spot.

model_development: What is the baseline metric we are trying to beat?
Who owns the decision on what accurate enough means for this domain?
What GPU or compute budget is allocated for training runs?
How many labelled examples does the ML engineer estimate are needed?
Is there a retraining budget post-launch?
hypercare: Who is the BAU owner for drift and incidents?

rule_lookup_not_ai.title: Use standard search
rule_lookup_not_ai.outcome: Let users find existing information accurately without training a predictive model.
steps: Confirm which records users need, which fields they search, and who may see each result
Decide whether exact database search is enough or a search index is needed
Build the query, filters, permissions, and result screen
Test common searches, missing records, access controls, and response time
Release to a small user group, measure failed searches, and improve the index or data

rule_automate_low_not_ai.title: Automate with workflow rules
rule_automate_low_not_ai.outcome: Remove repetitive manual work with transparent rules and an exception path.
steps: Map the current steps, decision rules, hand-offs, and exceptions
Agree which rules may run automatically and which cases require a person
Configure the workflow, business rules, notifications, and audit trail
Test normal cases, exceptions, permissions, rollback, and reporting
Pilot with one team, measure time saved and errors, then expand if the result is sound

rule_no_data_not_ai.title: Prepare the evidence first
rule_no_data_not_ai.outcome: Build a usable evidence base before choosing whether AI is appropriate.
steps: Define the decision or output and the measurable result that matters
Inventory possible data sources, owners, permissions, and retention limits
Capture representative examples and record the real outcomes consistently
Check coverage, quality, bias, and whether the data exists before the decision point
Return to Discovery when enough evidence exists to compare rules, standard software, and AI

default.title: Use a simpler non-AI solution
default.outcome: Solve the stated business need with the least complex reliable approach.
steps: Restate the required outcome and the users affected
Compare business rules, workflow software, database queries, reporting, and process redesign
Select the simplest option that meets the controls and success measure
Build and test a small pilot including exceptions and human ownership
Measure the result before adding more complexity

general.waterfall_ai_warning: Waterfall assumes stable requirements. Model work discovers constraints late. Prefer hybrid gates around iterative model cycles.
